title: Kuomintang
capsule: The Kuomintang (KMT, Chinese Nationalist Party), refounded by Sun Yat-sen in 1919 from the earlier Tongmenghui, became the dominant political force of Republican China after it reorganized with Soviet Comintern assistance in 1923 and established a revolutionary government in Canton. The KMT's military arm, the National Revolutionary Army under Chiang Kai-shek, launched the Northern Expedition in July 1926, unifying most of China under Nationalist government by 1928 and establishing the capital at Nanjing. The dataset attests the KMT's territorial-political geometry from 1917 to 1929, covering the Canton-based period through the early Nanjing decade; this span ends just as the Nationalist government completed nominal unification and the KMT's exclusive governing role became contested by the Chinese Communist Party and regional warlords. After 1949 the KMT retreated with the Republic of China government to Taiwan.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. KMT-controlled territory during the Northern Expedition period was fluid and contested; the dataset geometry for 1917–1929 necessarily represents approximate zones of KMT political predominance rather than precise administrative boundaries, given the overlapping warlord jurisdictions of the era.
